evidence: 'What adjectives describe the sun?' (Answers will vary, but may include: yellow, bright, fiery, shiny.) ... Tell students that today they will answer these two questions using pictures and words to show their thinking. Remind students to use the Adjectives anchor chart to describe what the sun and the moon look like.
rationale: The standard requires students to use descriptive words to craft engaging texts (C — construction mode). In the Closing and Assessment section, students independently write in their Sky notebooks, answering "What does the sun look like?" and "What does the moon look like?" using adjectives from the Adjectives anchor chart (e.g., "yellow, bright, fiery, shiny"). This meets the "use descriptive words" clause — students select and deploy adjectives in their own writing. However, the "craft engaging texts" clause is only partially met: the student writing is a brief, scaffolded notebook response to a teacher-posed question, not a purposefully crafted text aimed at engaging a reader. The adjective use adds descriptive quality, but the task structure (short prompt answers in a science notebook) does not fully realize the "craft engaging texts" expectation.
standard_raw_text: Use descriptive words to craft engaging texts. (C)

The investigate-questions clause is met when students work in pairs to model earth's rotation with flashlights to investigate "What makes day and night on earth?"
